questions.question: Write a design brief for the scrap-metal crane and explain which three questions it answers and what it deliberately leaves open.
questions.expected_answer: A suitable brief: design and make a model crane for a scrap-metal dealer that uses an electromagnet to lift ferrous scrap from a mixed pile, swing it to a separate bin and release it, so that steel is sorted from non-magnetic metals quickly and safely. It answers what is to be designed (a model crane with an electromagnet), for whom (the scrap dealer) and what it must do (lift only ferrous metal, move it and release it, quickly and safely). It deliberately leaves open the height, materials and whether the arm pivots or lifts, because those are design decisions for the sketching stage, and every word in it traces back to the investigation, such as ferrous and electromagnet.

questions.question: State the difference between a specification and a wish, and list at least four measurable specifications for the crane in order of importance.
questions.expected_answer: A specification is a measurable requirement that can be tested with a ruler, stopwatch, count or yes-or-no, whereas a wish such as "must be strong" has no instrument or number. Specifications in order of importance to the dealer: the electromagnet must pick up no copper, brass or aluminium from the mixed pile; it must release the whole load within one second of the switch opening; it must lift at least ten steel paper clips or a 20 gram washer; the arm must raise the load at least 150 millimetres and move it at least 200 millimetres sideways to a second bin; the crane must stand unaided while loaded; an indicator bulb must light whenever the magnet is on.

questions.question: Explain what constraints are, give the main constraints for the crane model, and describe the test that separates a constraint from a specification.
questions.expected_answer: Constraints are the limits placed on the designer rather than descriptions of what the product does. For the crane: materials limited to recycled card, dowel or skewers, string, a nail, insulated copper wire, one or two 1.5 volt cells, a push switch, a bulb, glue and tape; a base that fits an A4 sheet and a height of no more than 400 millimetres; four making periods; no cost beyond cells; safety rules of no mains electricity, a switch always in the circuit, no exposed sharp edges and no load swung over a person; and only the tools in the room. The test is to ask who the statement is about: if it describes the crane's performance it is a specification, if it describes the maker's resources and limits it is a constraint, and the two are written in separate columns.
